title: Momentum activation: battlecanvas for SE (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, high-velocity battlecanvas intended for SEs running short pilot or quick-POC engagements where momentum is the biggest risk. The goal: give a 3–4 minute technical pitch + 60s economic framing + pragmatic fallback play that gets an ‘OK to run’ decision fast.

Audience:
- Technical SEs and Field Sellers running 1–3 week pilots
- Platform/Integration architects considering Dedicated or Private
- Solutions engineers who need tight rebuttals for SLA/cost/latency concerns

One-liner to lead with (30s):
"Redwood makes inference predictable across hosted, reserved, and private footprints so your app stays responsive and cost-stable as load grows — and if you hit a capacity or quality problem, built-in fallbacks keep the experience live while we fix the root cause."

Top 3 value pillars (evidence-first):
1) Predictable latency under load — reference quick metric: p95 < 250ms on typical chat workloads using our small-reserved profile (see demo numbers below).
2) Cost control levers — batching, KV caching, and quantization profiles reduce token unit-cost by 20–55% depending on workload.
3) Graceful degradation — multi-tier routing + compatible fallbacks ensure SLA continuity when model/hardware constraints occur.

Quick 90s sales script (playbook starter):
- Hook (15s): "We help you ship inference without surprises — latency, cost, or outages."
- Why Redwood (30s): "Unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, smart routing that falls back to cheaper compatible variants, and observability that ties cost to token-level traces."
- Close (30s): "For a 2-week pilot we’ll run a small reserved pool, validate p95 and throughput against your sample traffic, and provide a rollback/fallback policy you control — if that sounds useful, let’s schedule a pilot runbook session."

Objection playbook: short rebuttals and exact scripts
1) "We can’t accept downtime / SLA risk"
  - Quick seller line: "Totally — our pilot config enforces fallback routing by default. If the primary variant crosses latency or error thresholds, traffic automatically shifts to a compatible variant or region while we investigate. We’ll demo failover in the pilot."
  - Tech note: show router policy snippet and canary timeline in demo.

2) "Cost looks high compared to self-hosting"
  - Seller line: "For initial velocity, the hosted/Dedicated mix reduces ops burden and often beats early self-hosted TCO. We’ll run a 7-day sample with billing simulation to show unit economics after batching and cache are applied."
  - Tech note: show Optimize suggestions and expected % reduction. Include quick example: chat bot 15k tokens/day -> 30% token-cost reduction via 2s batching + prefix cache.

3) "We’re regulated / need VPC or on-prem"
  - Seller line: "We support Private (VPC) deployments with customer-managed KMS and audit logs; we’ll scope a PoC for your compliance checklist in the pilot phase."

Demo checklist (10–12 minute live flow):
- Pre-demo: load sample dataset (own payload or sanitized copy)
- Step 1 (2 min): show API call and timing; live p95 and traces in Console
- Step 2 (3 min): increase concurrency with quick script; show autoscaling/throughput and cost deltas
- Step 3 (2 min): trigger fallback (simulate OOM/region throttle) and demonstrate traffic switching to variant + preserved session state where applicable
- Step 4 (2–3 min): show Optimize suggestions (batching cache settings) and projected cost improvement
- Callouts: bring up rollouts tab and canary metrics as proof of controlled deployment

Qualification checklist (quick filters for SEs):
- Current pilot goal: evaluate latency/quality or run a live mini-feature?
- Traffic profile: bursty? steady? average token length?
- Compliance: PII/regulated? need VPC or HSM?
- Success criteria (agreed before run): target p95, unit-cost delta threshold, and rollout acceptance criteria

Technical appendix (what to have ready):
- Sample traffic generator (attach link to small script)
- Small model variant suggestion table (recommended: Llama-2-13B-int8, coherence variant, opt for quantized fallback)
- Router policy example (pseudocode lines sellers can paste during demo)

Metrics & thresholds to call out (quick values to memorize):
- Low-latency target: p95 < 250–350ms for chat UI use cases
- Throughput: 200–800 tokens/sec per dedicated GPU (varies by model/quantization) — say ranges not absolutes
- Cost uplift guardrail for feature POC: expected <= 2x engineering infra spend vs. baseline, but typical batching/caching reduces to ~0.6–1.2x after tuning

Rapid A/B fallback script (operator-friendly):
- Canary: route 10% -> primary variant, observe 30m window; if p95 spikes > 2x baseline then shift to fallback and notify SE
- Emergency: auto-fallback on error rate > 2% within 5m

Seller-ready snippets to paste into Slack/email (30–60s templates):
- Pilot ask: "Can we run a 2-week pilot with a small reserved pool (4–8 vGPU units)? We’ll validate p95 under your sample traffic and build an automated fallback policy so you can ship without SLA surprises."
- Post-demo follow-up: "Attached: demo recording, router policy snippet, and a one-page cost simulation. Next step: align on pilot success criteria and sign-off on data-handling controls."

Risk notes / failure modes to surface:
- Large context windows may push p95 beyond targets; mitigation: recommend KV caching + truncation strategies
- Heavy multimodal payloads require specialized quantization and additional GPU memory — call SRE early in scoping
- QA: model quality regressions after quantization — tie a small eval set to the pilot and alert on regression delta > 5% ROUGE/utility metric

Rollout/TODOs (owner + assignees):
- [Aisha] Draft pilot-runbook and instrumentation checklist (due: 2025-11-10)
- [Liam] Prepare demo traffic generator and billing sim (due: 2025-11-14)
- [Sofia] Create fallback policy snippet + brief video capture (due: 2025-11-16)
- [Raj] Validate Private deployment checklist for regulated pilot (due: 2025-11-18)

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep demo under 15 minutes; avoid deep infra dive unless asked
- Emphasize controllability: sellers love deterministic levers they can show to prospects (percent routes, canary windows, auto-fallback thresholds)
- Add a one-pager cost quick-sim (excel) that takes tokens/day, avg length, batching to output estimated monthly cost — SEs ask for this every time

End: short checklist to save as a quick card for SEs to carry into calls:
- 3-min pitch + 90s script ready
- Demo runbook + traffic loaded
- Fallback policy copied into console
- Pilot success criteria emailed to prospect

(Working doc — expect edits. Use linked artifacts for deeper design notes.)
